PROVED — THE QUORUM SIGNATURE GATE HAS AN ADDRESS. A node proved by human judgment can now actually be sealed. node_classes/concept-piece.json specified this gate on 2026-07-15 and ZERO concept-piece VALIDATIONs existed in the ten days since — not because a reviewer was slow, but because validations_path_for derived a seal's address from a PROOF FILE path and a concept-piece has no proof file, so the single write-door could not physically accept the record. The gate was never awaiting a signature; it was awaiting an ADDRESS, and CC repeatedly reported the former, which is what kept it stuck. Closed with validations_path_for_artifact (the seal lands beside the artifact, derived not chosen, Law 5) and cairn/devices/tester/quorum.py. Same ratified eight fields, same persist_validation, no rival door (Law 6) — only the addressing was ever missing. Physics: a notary who also reviewed is REFUSED (verdict and seal are different hands; a self-seal is the hollow build, Law 8), a signature with no restated-back understanding is REFUSED (a rubber stamp proves someone clicked, not that anyone read), a quorum means DISTINCT hands, and a rejection is a recorded RED that kicks back (CP2), not an exception. PROVED — THE VALIDATION TRAIL'S DOOR IS NOW THE ONLY PATH (ticket validation-store-door-is-the-only-path, P1, drained from the live trouble). The trail was a record of truth declared APPEND-ONLY by its door and stored as a plain 0644 JSON file: a hand-write destroyed a proof's whole seal history silently and permanently, and looked exactly like a fresh seal (Law 7's worst direction). Closed in three layers that answer three different failure modes — the MODE BIT (0444) stops the accident at the open(); the CHAIN (a door-minted trail_link per record, sha256 over the trail beneath it plus the record itself) makes the deliberate loud, and standing() refuses a broken trail rather than reading a verdict out of it, so harbor_master clears nothing on it; the CORPUS SCAN refuses a second writer at BUILD time rather than at runtime. THE PROOF KILLED THE FIRST DESIGN: a tolerated unlinked prefix ("prehistory") is indistinguishable from a total overwrite, which is the exact destroy-the-history shape the trouble named — a tolerance is a forger's costume whenever the forger can produce the thing tolerated. So the 73 legacy trails were ADOPTED instead: 220 entries linked, all verify, idempotent, and adoption REFUSES to re-link a tampered trail. quorum.record_verdict now returns what LANDED, not what it built (the assembled dict was a second, unlinked copy — the rival-source-of-truth defect MethodRegistry already was). NAMED, NOT GLOSSED: the bytes stay writable to the same uid, nothing here un-destroys a trail, and git carries only the exec bit so a fresh clone lands 0644 until the door next appends — the chain is the half that survives a clone. 9/9 teeth (6 new), quorum 9/9, corpus 86 · 85 green · 1 red over four consecutive runs.

The disposition is the corpus's own mechanism, not a paragraph — a forwarding order on this ticket naming the successor that carries the question, both ends checked in the world, exactly as watchme-emits-a-probe disposed of the renames its own decompose ordered. note: A VALIDATION IS ONE CURRENT RECORD, NOT A TRAIL — Akien's ruling of 2026-08-16 built and proved. persist_validation REPLACES the standing record, and a DIFFERING incoming verdict raises a trouble through TroubleDevice BEFORE the replace lands: announce-then-write is the whole of what makes the collapse legal under Law 7, because announcing after would let a crash lose the change AND the record it replaced, while announcing first can at worst raise a false alarm. The one-time collapse printed 'collapsed 54 files; dropped 193 superseded records into git'; the corpus now reads 91 files, 91 records, max 1 per file, and only 2 of the 54 held a verdict change at all — the trail was 52-of-54 repetition, which is what the ruling's 'it tends to create noise' names. THE CHAIN RETIRED WITH WHAT IT PROTECTED: _link_for was an importable pure function, so anyone could mint a link that verified — measured, with a forger's trail standing green — and the unforgeability was never bought. What the chain bought was deletion-detection, i.e. the append-only-ness this ticket spends, so it retired with it. Four honest layers remain (the 0444 mode bit, the build-time second-writer scan, source_fingerprint, git), and the new instrument is strictly harder to fake than the link it replaced: producing a two-record file REQUIRES doing the exact thing being watched for. Verdict artifact verdict-20260816T142450-26f633a38b9a.json answers all 7 validate criteria pass, with 9 of 10 hypotheses confirmed and 1 KILLED. THE CORRECTIONS THIS CROSSING CARRIES, because a green that hides them teaches nothing. (1) TOOTH COUNT: the PROVEME note two crossings back says '13/13 teeth' and the file measures 14 — a hand's miscount, and the proof's own roster floor had been written 13 from the same miscount, leaving room for exactly the one disappearance a floor exists to catch. History is append-only so that note stands; the floor is raised to 14, the reason is recorded in-file, and this record is the correction. (2) A SIBLING PROBE RETIRED: the_door_is_the_only_path_in_practice counted entries carrying no trail_link, a key now written by nothing; the first fix — keep it and re-instrument it — was measured wrong in-build (two probes, one number, one clearing condition: probescan's own REPEATS class), so it is gone and its question is carried by the armed probe, with the reason in that probe's docstring and a forwarding order on the ticket naming the successor, both ends checked in the world. (3) ONE UNEXPLAINED TRANSIENT: the first corpus sweep printed 111 proofs / 108 green / 3 red and the third red's identity was not captured because only the tail was kept; three later sweeps print 109/2, the two pre-existing reds (test_route.py, test_watchme_spec.py, both already standing troubles). Recorded rather than rounded off — the method fix is to tee the whole sweep. (4) THE FIRST DRAFT OF THE ANNOUNCEMENT GUARD keyed on class-space and passed its own proofs while being wrong: quorum.seal addresses CairnCommons concept-pieces, so it would have silenced every human-proved review flip. The guard predicate is the TEMP ROOT, and the charter's falsifier now names that mistake as clause (8). LIVE FIRE: a green-then-red pair sealed at a real class-space address raised validation-verdict-changed-live-fire-artifact in the real trouble store, and `bin/cmd/slate` rendered it at the top of the session banner — the human surface the criterion demanded. Cleared through TroubleDevice.clear afterwards; the scratch artifact was never committed.

The cost is on the record at every seal — evidence.instance_seal.scratch carries apparent bytes AND disk bytes AND entry count, because the old snapshot was 136MB of content sitting in 424MB of 4KB blocks: apparent alone understates 3x, disk alone hides that the cost is entry COUNT. Its tooth wrote one line into an isolated trail and asserted trail_misses >= 1 — a bound BOTH trails meet — so for two months it passed on the live trail's borrowed lines and never on the line it wrote. The seal did not break that proof; it removed the accident the proof was passing on. note: PROVED. The hollow verb reverts a file and reads the teeth — and the defect this voyage found was not that it failed, it was that it SUCCEEDED WRONGLY. Two causes, and only the second one mattered. (1) git exports GIT_INDEX_FILE=.git/index — a RELATIVE path — plus GIT_PREFIX= into every hook, and the pre-commit hook runs the reseal door, which runs proofs as subprocesses that inherit it; scratch_worktree died loudly under that env in 0.12s, which is the honest failure and was fixed first. (2) hollow._restore, a `git -C <worktree> checkout -- <rel>`, resolved against the CALLER's index instead of the worktree's, did nothing, said nothing, and returned nothing to look at. So file N stayed reverted while file N+1 was measured, N+1's teeth redded for a reason that had nothing to do with N+1, that red read as 'a declared tooth checks this file', and A FILE THAT REALLY WAS HOLLOW WAS REPORTED ok — a hollow read as green, manufactured inside the catcher whose whole job is catching one (Law 8: a false green gets leaned on by a peer; that is why it is worse than a red). `git -C <root>` is not a defence anywhere, because GIT_DIR and its siblings outrank it everywhere. THE FIX IS TWO THINGS, and the second is the one that generalises: _git_env became public git_env() and every git call in the tester that means 'the repository I am pointing at' now takes it (3 in scratch.py, 4 in hollow.py, the fixtures in test_hollow.py); and _restore RAISES HollowUnmeasurable when the checkout fails, because the next thing that stops a checkout will not be an env var and the verb must not go on measuring past it (Law 3: a measurement that could not be taken may not travel home through the same return as a clean one). A 13th tooth pins that raise, and it is deliberately not coupled to the env var that revealed it — it makes the checkout fail by pointing at a directory that is no repository. Mutation-verified: stub the guard to `if False:` and it fails; restore it and it passes. THE LINE THAT IS NOT OVER-APPLIED, recorded in the docstring because it is easy to get wrong: reseal.staged_files must NOT scrub. Under `git commit -a` git writes a TEMPORARY index and points GIT_INDEX_FILE at it, so the hook's staged set lives there and nowhere else; scrubbing would read the pre-`-a` index and reseal the wrong proofs. A call meaning 'the repository I am pointing at' scrubs; a call meaning 'the index my caller is committing' must not. MEASURED: test_hollow.py under GIT_INDEX_FILE=.git/index GIT_PREFIX= went from 4 failed to 12 passed in 311.64s, and seals 13 teeth_green / 0 teeth_red. Live fire `cairn test --seal --hollow 9579a6f9cec6` at HEAD 3159682: 8 measured · 0 hollow · 2 skipped, exit 0, 'SEALED — hollow evidence landed on 3 of 3 standing validation(s)', wall clock 2m7s against the ticket's 5-minute WRONG INTENT threshold — so the shared-worktree redesign that clause calls for is not owed. All three seals carry exactly the eight ratified fields and evidence.hollow['9579a6f9cec6'] over 8 files. OWED, MEASURED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE: 12 proof files and 11 non-proof modules shell `git -C <root>` and only 2 scrub — test_inspector.py, test_history_integrity.py and test_forwarding_derivation.py bare-inherit, test_ruling.py inherits os.environ straight into git. They are out of this voyage's bounds for a structural reason, not a tired one: git_env lives in cairn.devices.tester.scratch, so build_inspector's and ruling's proofs cannot import it without a cross-device import (ruled: only db_domain). Its right home is a tool, and picking that rung is design work, not a patch.
